sourceMathEvidence: The stem intersects |2x−1|≤x+2 with 5x²−12x+2≤0 and asks for the sum of the common interval endpoints.
solutionMathEvidence: The absolute-value condition gives [−1/3,3]. The quadratic gives [(6−√26)/5,(6+√26)/5], which is wholly inside [−1/3,3], so both endpoints and their sum 12/5 come solely from the quadratic interval.

crossConcepts.reason: Removing the absolute-value condition leaves the same decisive quadratic interval and endpoint sum, so CC_INEQUALITY_ABSOLUTE_VALUE fails the counterfactual gate. CC_INEQUALITY_QUADRATIC is already the primary L3 and would duplicate it.

integrationPattern.reason: Under the canonical definition, NONE applies when the primary taxonomy alone resolves the item. The absolute-value interval is checked for containment but does not change the quadratic interval or answer; there is no necessary second concept to apply sequentially or interdependently.
